learning_outcomes.text: Gains the ability to look at culture on an analytical thinking ground comparatively.
Can interpret current cultural issues based on historical data.
Can observe the cultural environment from a broad perspective.
Can discuss cultural policies and cultural institutions.
Can conduct research, approach issues from multiple perspectives, and draw conclusions.

syllabus_topics: Changing life and Ottoman world in the 19th century
Impact of urbanization on culture and art, examples of Paris, London, New York, and Istanbul
Role of 20th-century art movements and groups in the development of cultural policy: Expressionism, Cubism, and Futurism
Role of 20th-century art movements and groups in the development of cultural policy: Expressionism, Cubism, and Futurism
"Art for Art's Sake" Russian Constructivism: Rodchenko, Tatlin, Lissitzky, and Gabo. State and Art
New forms of governance and the problem of culture emerging from the concepts of nation and public
Institutionalization of culture and the beginning of cultural strategies in the new Turkish Republic
Cultural imperialisms in the first half of the 20th century
Cultural policies of the Republic I
Cultural policies of the Republic II
UNESCO structure and United Nations cultural programs: Venice, Helsinki, and Mexico City Conferences
New era in cultural policies: World Conference on Cultural Policies in Mexico City 1982
